source.author: lucan
source.text: Nec, quamvis viridi lactetur robore, lentas Ignis agit vires: teda sed raptus ab omni Consequitur nigri spatiosa volumina fumi: Nec solum silvas, sed saxa iugentia solvit, Et crudae putri fluxerunt pulvere cautes.
source.text_original: Nec, quamvis viridi lactetur robore, lentas / Ignis agit vires: teda sed raptus ab omni / Consequitur nigri spatiosa volumina fumi: / Nec solum silvas, sed saxa iugentia solvit, / Et crudae putri fluxerunt pulvere cautes.
source.text_english: Nor, though it be nourished by fresh strength, does fire exert sluggish force: rather, once seized, it follows after the broad coils of black smoke from every pine-torch; it not only dissolves woods, but towering rocks, and raw cliffs have flowed away into rotten dust.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Protulit ut crinem densis luctatus in extis ignis et escendit salientia viscera tauri, ecce sacer totusque dei per litora Mopsus immanis visu vittamque comamque per auras surgentem laurusque rotat.
reuse.text_original: Protulit ut crinem densis luctatus in extis / ignis et escendit salientia viscera tauri, / ecce sacer totusque dei per litora Mopsus / immanis visu vittamque comamque per auras / surgentem laurusque rotat.
reuse.text_english: As the fire, struggling amid the crowded entrails, brought forth the hair and climbed over the quivering innards of the bull, behold, the sacred Mopsus, wholly possessed by the god, terrible to see, was moving along the shore, his fillet and hair rising through the air, and he was brandishing laurel branches.
